newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end lower in mixed trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end lower in mixed trade.

text.p: Swedish shares closed lower in mixed trade on Monday with the market lacking any strong direction.
The Stockholm general index slipped 0.07 percent to 2,636.26 after shares worth 4.01 billion crowns changed hands.

The main focus was on the bank sector which rose 0.76 percent amid continuing merger talk. Nordbanken chief executive Hans Dalborg told newspaper Dagens Nyheter a merger with S-E-Banken would be good.
Nordbanken closed two crowns higher at 265 crowns while S-E-Banken edged up 0.5 to 82.50.
Blue chips stocks ended lower with telecoms group Ericsson losing 3.5 to 236.5 crowns in line with a weaker technology sector in the U.S.. Drugs major Astra closed 1.5 lower at 355 crowns.
"But it was a really quiet day," one broker said.
Engineer Sandvik posted a 21 percent fall in 1996 profits which was worse than the market expected. Its share price ended 2.5 crowns lower at 188 crowns.
Trade was strong in building group Skanska ahead of the company posting its 1996 results on Tuesday. Its shares rose three crowns to 342 crowns.
Other companies due to report on Wednesday included building group NCC and ferry operator Stena Line.
